newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - NOV 22.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - NOV 22.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--The Greek government is on course for collision with the other European Union countries if Monday's Council of Foreign Ministers attempts to change its July decision calling on Ankara to respect the territorial integrity of EU member-states and its external borders. Foreign Minister Theodoros Pangalos yesterday said it would be "monstrous" to send the message that Turkey "can blackmail Europe and conduct any policy without consequence". Yesterday, Turkish warplanes violated Greek air space 18 times.
--International houses are combing through the transactions of 29 brokerage firms on eight listed companies.
--State titles will remain tax-free to foreign investors. The government however is working hard to ensure that this does not provide a way for Greek investors to avoid tax.

--Pangalos issues his warning ahead of Monday's General Affairs Council meeting: Either the European Union will call on Turkey to fall into line with international law and to seek recourse to the International Court at The Hague on the islet of Imia or Greece will block unanimity on Monday. There will be no package deals, he says categorically to journalists yesterday.

--The Day of the Gypsies. Furious at the senseless killing of a father of six by police, Gypsies yesterday marched on Parliament to condemn the indifference of the state and the ease with which they become targets for police bullets.
--The finance ministry's indexation of the tax scale and the abolition of tax exemptions will force even the have-nots to put their hands deep into their pockets.
--Athenians got a jolt last night when the Attica prefecture was swayed by a tremor registering 3.8 on the Richter scale. The epicentre was Kalamaki, five kms south of Athens.

--Islands and border regions are included in the objective evaluation of real estate as of Monday. The inclusion of the 61 regions will help in determining the amount of tax to pay on the new real estate tax and other charges.

--Two Greek air force Mirage F-1s formed an impromptu honour guard for Defence Minister Akis Tsohatzopoulos as he flew to Cyprus yesterday as soon as control was informed that Turkish fighter planes were headed in the same direction.

--Real estate market experts say the government's new tax - to be calculated on what is held by families rather than individuals - will lead taxpayers to bogus divorces to protect their property. Other effects they say, will be an increase in rentals and a fall in building activity.
--Opposition New Democracy leader Miltiades Evert says the government's new wages for officers is crumbs and calls for pay levels to be brought up to that for judges.
--Euthanasia is an open secret, a Panteion University study says. The study reports claims of newborns born with Downs Syndrome being given medicines to die.
